---
title: "Under a normal model, what proportion falls below a cutoff?"
---

## Question

Under a normal model, what proportion falls below a cutoff?

## Work through it

Check whether a normal approximation is appropriate; specify mean, standard deviation and cutoff; compute the lower cumulative probability.

## Worked example: airquality

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("airquality")
mu <- mean(d$Temp)
sigma <- sd(d$Temp)
result <- ru_apply("normal_left_tail", mu=mu, sigma=sigma,
                   threshold=75, assume_normal=TRUE)
stopifnot(result>0,result<1)
```

The calculation fits illustrative normal parameters to recorded daily temperatures. It predicts a model area below 75°F, which need not equal the actual proportion below 75°F.

## Adapt to another question

```r
ru_apply("normal_left_tail", mu=your_mean, sigma=your_sd, threshold=your_cutoff, assume_normal=TRUE)
```

If you want the observed share instead of model probability, use mean(d$Temp<75,na.rm=TRUE).

Check the input conditions with `ru_plan("normal_left_tail")` before treating a calculation as an inference.
